facts.statement: Arganasuchus is an extinct genus of rauisuchian archosaur.
facts.quote: Arganasuchus is an extinct genus of "rauisuchian" (loricatan) archosaur.

facts.statement: The genus Arganasuchus contains only one known species, Arganasuchus dutuiti.
facts.quote: It is known from a single species, Arganasuchus dutuiti.

facts.statement: Remains initially thought to belong to Ticinosuchus were identified as the distinct genus Arganasuchus in 2007 based on unique pubis and maxilla features.
facts.quote: Though its remains were initially referred to Ticinosuchus when discovered during the 1970s, in 2007 it was identified as a distinct genus with unique features of the pubis and maxilla.

facts.statement: Jean-Michel Dutuit first reported fossils of Arganasuchus in 1979, initially attributing them to Ticinosuchus.
facts.quote: Fossils of Arganasuchus were first reported by Jean-Michel Dutuit in 1979, who referred a maxilla, dentary, femur, and fibula to Ticinosuchus.

facts.statement: Fossils were found in the Timezgadiouine Formation in the Argana Basin of Morocco, dated to the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: This geological formation, which is found in the Argana Basin of Morocco, may have been deposited in the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic period.

facts.statement: Arganasuchus lived between 237 and 227.3 million years ago during the Carnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: Arganasuchus is considered a carnivore because it possessed large, knife-shaped teeth.
facts.quote: Arganasuchus is considered a carnivore due to its large, knife-shaped teeth.

facts.statement: The maxilla of Arganasuchus held at least 12 large, knife-like teeth in deep sockets covered by interdental plates.
facts.quote: The maxilla has a straight lower edge with at least 12 large, knife-like teeth set in deep sockets and covered by interdental plates.

facts.statement: The maxilla of Arganasuchus has a Y-shape similar to that of Batrachotomus and Fasolasuchus.
facts.quote: The maxilla as a whole is Y-shaped like Batrachotomus and Fasolasuchus.

facts.statement: Arganasuchus has an unusually long anterior process on its maxilla that forms the stem of its Y-shaped structure.
facts.quote: The maxilla also has an unusually long anterior process (forward branch), forming the "stem" of the Y shape.

facts.statement: Preserved front jaw fragments indicate that Arganasuchus had at least 14 teeth in its lower jaw.
facts.quote: Although the rear of the lower jaw is unknown, enough of the front half was preserved to indicate that at least 14 teeth were present.

facts.statement: Arganasuchus exhibited an alternating tooth replacement scheme common among archosaurs.
facts.quote: Arganasuchus has an alternating tooth replacement scheme, like many other archosaurs.

facts.statement: The pubis bone is considered one of the most unusual and unique skeletal features of Arganasuchus.
facts.quote: The pubis is among the most unusual and unique bones in Arganasuchus.

facts.statement: The size and orientation of the acetabulum on the pubis is a unique defining feature (autapomorphy) of Arganasuchus.
facts.quote: The size and orientation of the acetabulum on the pubis is an autapomorphy (unique defining feature) of Arganasuchus.

facts.statement: The femur of Arganasuchus is large and robust, featuring a prominent fourth trochanter and a smaller knob that may indicate diseased bone.
facts.quote: The femur is large and robust, with a prominent knob-like fourth trochanter overlooking a smaller knob which may be an area of diseased bone.

facts.statement: Arganasuchus is universally classified as a rauisuchian, a group of large carnivorous Triassic pseudosuchians.
facts.quote: Arganasuchus is universally considered a "rauisuchian", a grouping of large carnivorous pseudosuchians (crocodile-line archosaurs) from the Triassic.

facts.statement: The group Rauisuchia is currently viewed as a paraphyletic grade of archosaurs rather than a natural clade.
facts.quote: However, "Rauisuchia" is currently considered to be a paraphyletic grade of archosaurs incrementally closer to crocodilians, rather than a clade (a natural grouping defined by shared relations).

facts.statement: It is debated how Arganasuchus fits into modern crocodilian ancestry classifications, leaving its precise relationship to other rauisuchians poorly understood.
facts.quote: Although most frequently compared with loricatans, Arganasuchus has yet to be properly incorporated into this newer understanding of crocodilian ancestry, and as a result its classification relative to other "rauisuchians" is poorly understood.

facts.statement: There is no scientific consensus on the precise phylogenetic affinities of Arganasuchus despite various analytical attempts.
facts.quote: Some phylogenetic analyses have attempted to deal with Arganasuchus, although there is no consensus on its precise affinities.

facts.statement: Arganasuchus belongs to the family Rauisuchidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Rauisuchidae

facts.statement: Arganasuchus is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
